              example: 'SPR-SMI-0007-M26'
              readOnly: true
            membershipPoints:
              title: Membership points
              description: The owner's membership points, assigned on creation. Points start at 0
                and accumulate 2 when an email is present, 1 when namesakeCount is 0, 2 when the
                owner belongs to a household of 3 or more, and 3 when tenure exceeds one elapsed
                fiscal year.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 3
              readOnly: true
            membershipLevel:
              title: Membership level
              description: The owner's numeric membership level, derived from membershipPoints as

              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 1
              maximum: 4
              example: 2
              readOnly: true
            locality:
              title: Locality
              description: The region derived from the owner's city using the fixed
                city-to-region table (Sydney->NSW, Melbourne->VIC, Brisbane->QLD), or
                'UNKNOWN' when the city is not in the table.
              type: string
              example: 'NSW'
              readOnly: true
            timezone:
              title: Timezone
              description: The IANA timezone name derived from the owner's locality/region
                using the fixed region-to-timezone table (NSW->Australia/Sydney,
                VIC->Australia/Melbourne, QLD->Australia/Brisbane); absent when the owner
                has no known region.

) engine=InnoDB;

) engine=InnoDB;

  UNIQUE KEY uni_username_role (role,username),
  KEY fk_username_idx (username),

) engine=InnoDB;

content.text:
The full suite (the single `AcceptanceTest`) builds and passes. 

The implementation is complete. Here's a summary of what I did to satisfy the spec — *"A new owner's membershipLevel cannot exceed one above the current maximum membershipLevel among their household members; return the capped membershipLevel. With no existing household member no cap applies."*

**`Owner.java` (model)**
- Added a persisted `membershipLevelCap` field (`@Column(name = "membership_level_cap")`) with accessors — this stores the ceiling computed at creation so it survives the round trip and is applied on every `GET`.
- Added static `cappedMembershipLevel(int level, Integer cap)` — the single definition of the ceiling: returns the level unchanged when `cap` is `null`, otherwise `Math.min(level, cap)`.
- `getMembershipLevel()` now returns the points-derived level held to that ceiling.

**`OwnerRestControllerV1.java` (create path)**
- Added `householdMembershipLevelCap(householdId)`: over the existing, non-deleted household members (computed before the new owner is saved, so it excludes the new owner), it stamps each member's household count, takes the max `membershipLevel`, and returns `max + 1`; returns `null` when the household has no existing members (no cap).
- `createOwner` sets this cap on the owner right before persisting.

**Schema** — added the `membership_level_cap` column to all four schemas (h2, hsqldb, mysql, postgres); tests run on hsqldb with `ddl-auto=none`, so the column had to be declared explicitly.

The capped `membershipLevel` flows out through the existing MapStruct mapping (property-name match) with no mapper change needed, and the OpenAPI `membershipLevel` field already bounds the value at `1..4`.
